fragments.text: > Galvanic Vestibular Stimulation (GVS) is a technology that directly affects a user's vestibular system by altering their sense of balance and direction through electrical stimulation via electrodes placed on the mastoid bones behind each ear. message.body: > However, in walking users, when their head is pitched forward, it causes them to turn smoothly from their planned trajectory in the anodal direction (Fig c, d). A VR player equipped with the GVS device, and a non-VR player who can control the GVS stimulus (time, duration, direction) to steer the walking trajectory of the VR player, work together in an 'escape the room' like game.
